questions.question: The "Arc of Riolan" is a mesenteric collateral pathway that connects:
questions.detail: It is an important meandering mesenteric collateral seen in the setting of proximal arterial occlusion.

questions.question: Which collateral pathway connects the SMA and IMA along the periphery of the colon?
questions.detail: This runs along the mesenteric border of the colon.

questions.question: "Median Arcuate Ligament Syndrome" (MALS) causes narrowing of which vessel?
questions.detail: Compression is caused by the ligament of the diaphragm, characteristically worsening during expiration.

questions.question: Acute mesenteric ischemia caused by an embolus (e.g., from the heart) typically lodges where in the SMA?
choices: At the exact origin from the aorta
Distal to the origin of the middle colic artery
questions.detail: Emboli usually lodge 3–10 cm from the origin, often sparing the proximal branches.

questions.question: "Nutcracker syndrome" refers to the compression of the left renal vein between:
questions.detail: This compression leads to left-sided flank pain, hematuria, and occasionally a varicocele in males.

questions.question: "May-Thurner syndrome" (iliac vein compression syndrome) involves compression of the left common iliac vein by the:
questions.detail: This predisposition leads to chronic left leg swelling and DVT.

questions.question: "Pelvic Congestion Syndrome" is associated with chronic pelvic pain and the presence of:
choices: Dilation of the ovarian veins and pelvic varices
questions.detail: This results from venous valvular insufficiency and reflux.

questions.question: Polyarteritis nodosa (PAN) classically presents on visceral angiography with:
choices: Numerous tiny peripheral aneurysms (microaneurysms) in the kidneys or mesentery
questions.detail: PAN is a necrotizing vasculitis of small- and medium-sized arteries.

questions.question: Which vessel serves as the critical landmark for differentiating "upper" from "lower" GI bleeding for interventionalists?
questions.detail: This anatomical landmark defines the junction where GI bleeding sources are categorized.

questions.question: A "tangled" appearance of high-velocity, low-resistance vessels in the uterus on Doppler is suggestive of:
questions.detail: These are rare but can cause life-threatening hemorrhage.

questions.question: "Renal artery stenosis" caused by fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) classically appears as:
choices: A smooth, focal narrowing at the origin
A "string of beads" in the mid-to-distal renal artery
questions.detail: FMD typically involves the mid-to-distal segments, unlike atherosclerosis which favors the origin.

questions.question: In the evaluation of "Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia," how many of the three main mesenteric vessels are typically involved?
choices: All three plus the renal arteries
questions.detail: Because of the extensive collateral network, single-vessel disease is rarely symptomatic.

questions.question: The "CLASH" mnemonic for Polyarteritis nodosa includes which of the following?
choices: Chronic illness, Lung, Arteries, Spleen, Hypertension
questions.detail: PAN is strongly associated with Hepatitis B and hypertension.

questions.question: What is the normal "resistive index" (RI) for the segmental renal arteries?
questions.detail: An RI >0.7 is non-specific but may indicate obstruction or medical renal disease.

questions.question: Cavernous transformation of the portal vein is the result of:
questions.detail: This represents the formation of periportal collaterals to bypass the clot.
